correctness.rationale: PASS for the stated iid-across-iterations two-component, equal-step, planar bilinear model. With J²=-I, the one-step product is ((1-eta²uv)I-eta v J); its squared norm has no cross term. Averaging the complete 2-by-2 fixed-uniform-marginal coupling matrix gives affine q(theta), so a linear objective selects endpoint coupling except at eta²=2/(a+b)². Exact polynomial factorization P(r)/r²=(r+1/r)²-2(r+1/r)-4 orders the three stability thresholds, yielding iff 1<r<phi+sqrt(phi), plus strict rational witness at a=1,b=2,eta=3/5: 751/625,109/100,1223/1250. Independently recomputed 36 rational parameter/coupling checks; these checks alone are not an all-parameter proof.
residual_risks: Only mean-square decay, not almost-sure convergence; iid pairs across iterations essential.

value.rationale: PASS. The bounded but natural optimal-coupling question distinguishes two conventional two-oracle stochastic extragradient schemes from a third equally costly coupling. A sharp explicit threshold and rational strict-separation witness are informative about sampling correlation and mean-square stability rather than mere normalization or a textbook sign check.
